findings.title: Retry-count delete filter deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany uses OR with a second branch of only retryCount gt 1 with no method: SMS constraint (lines 29-45). Once any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) has retryCount > 1 it will be deleted by this SMS cron job, even if it is scheduled for the future and unrelated to SMS. This is data loss beyond the intended SMS cleanup; the retryCount branch must also be scoped to method SMS (and likely scheduled: false).

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
findings.body: Both failure paths update with data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read at the start of the cron run (lines 184 and 195) instead of an atomic increment. If two cron invocations or overlapping executions process the same reminder, one increment overwrites the other, so failures are under-counted and bad numbers are retried forever. Use increment: 1.

findings.title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount, retries forever
findings.body: RetryCount is only incremented when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws, inside if (message?.length && sendTo). When sendTo is missing (e.g. invalid/missing phone number) or message is empty, the loop does nothing and leaves the reminder unscheduled with unchanged retryCount. That reminder will be re-fetched on every cron run forever, which is exactly the infinite-rescheduling problem the PR claims to fix for invalid numbers.
